14	CASE OD2-HO-SEQ-2 (SEQ, cross-domain): Expiry dates a year too late on Veltranol cartons at Ashcombe Packaging, Wrexley
15	Setting: Ashcombe Packaging Services' Wrexley site is a contract packager running four blister-and-carton lines (Lines 1-4). Each line has an Inkora TJ-5 inkjet printer that prints lot and expiry on cartons, and a camera that inspects every carton. A line integration service, PackBridge (supplied by Corvane Systems), takes product data from the site ERP and pre-fills each print job. Several changes were made at the site between late September and October 2026.
16	Presenting request: The client's quality lead asks for an independent view. What caused the wrong expiry dates on Veltranol cartons? Is the site director's plan right? What should the site do now? You may collect at most two further items of evidence.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Deviation DV-26-114 opening record, QA, 12 Nov 2026 (system-record): Deviation DV-26-114, opened 12 Nov 2026 (QA). Kestrel Distribution's goods-in system rejected three lots of Veltranol 20 mg tablets, 28s (VT-2641, VT-2644, VT-2652), because the printed expiry was later than the maximum shelf life in Kestrel's product file. Cartons and 2D codes read EXP 10/2029. The approved batch records, generated from the ERP batch master, state EXP 10/2028 (24 months from bulk manufacture). All three lots were packed on Line 3, night shift, 9-23 Oct. Veltranol is the only product Kestrel buys from the site. Immediate action: the three lots are on hold and Kestrel is quarantining the stock it received. Status of other Veltranol lots: not yet reviewed.
19	E2 [stage S1] Email from Gareth Lindqvist, Site Director, to the client quality lead, 13 Nov 2026 (leadership-account): 'I want to be straight with you. All three lots came off Line 3 nights, which is where our new agency cohort started on 30 September. Setup on these lines lets the operator overwrite the pre-filled expiry, and our night supervisor tells me the new starters weren't always confident with that screen. I'm satisfied this is a people issue. This week I'm removing the agency operators from labelling duties and issuing formal warnings, and we'll retrain everyone. I don't expect you'll see this again.'
20	E3 [stage S1] Site change-control log summary, 15 Sep - 31 Oct 2026 (change-record): CC-301 (28 Sep): Inkora TJ-5 printer firmware 4.2 to 4.3 on all four line printers, to fix intermittent dropping of the final lot-code character. CC-305 (30 Sep): six agency operators added to the night shift on Lines 3 and 4. CC-309 (1-24 Oct): Regulatory Affairs material-master update, 12 edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. CC-311 (1 Oct): camera font re-teach, Line 3. No changes to PackBridge (line integration service) were recorded in the period.
21	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Dana Whitcombe, night-shift supervisor, 13 Nov 2026 (manager-account): 'At job setup PackBridge fills in the lot number and expiry. The operator checks the printer screen against the work-order printout, which also comes out of PackBridge, then presses Confirm or overrides with a reason code. Operators can't touch PackBridge or the ERP, only the printer screen. Some of the agency lads were slow on that screen in their first fortnight. I had to talk two of them through it. The camera reads every carton and kicks out anything smudged or cut short, about three in a thousand. It checks the print matches the job. It doesn't know the batch record. The printers log every job's setup values if QA want them.'
22	E5 [stage S1] Email from Corvane Systems support (PackBridge vendor) to site QA, 14 Nov 2026 (vendor-account): 'PackBridge reads product master data from your ERP when a job is created and works out expiry as manufacture date plus shelf life. Master-data records carry a valid-from date, and PackBridge only ever uses the value in effect on the job date. It cannot send a future value to the line. No other site has reported date errors on this version. We suggest you look at manual overrides at the printer.'
23	E6 [stage S1] QA manager note to file, 14 Nov 2026 (manager-account): 'I wouldn't assume this started in October. Kestrel only switched on its shelf-life check at goods-in on 1 October, so before that nobody outside would have caught a late expiry. Our in-process checks compare the carton to the work order, so they wouldn't have caught it either. I'd treat everything since the last audit as suspect until shown otherwise.'
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Inkora printer job records, Veltranol 20 mg, all lines, 1 Jun - 10 Nov 2026 - Inkora TJ-5 job database export, pulled by Engineering, 15 Nov 2026 (log): Export of 47 Veltranol jobs (28s and 56s) on Lines 1-4. Each job record has: date and shift, line, operator ID, expiry received in the PackBridge payload, shelf-life basis in the payload (SHELF_LIFE_M), operator override (Y/N), expiry printed, camera result.
26	- 2 Jun to 3 Oct (30 jobs): SHELF_LIFE_M = 24, and expiry matches the batch record. This includes 4 jobs after the 28 Sep firmware change, 3 of them on Line 3 nights, 30 Sep to 3 Oct, set up by agency operators.
27	- 4 Oct 22:10 to 10 Nov (17 jobs): SHELF_LIFE_M = 36, and expiry is 12 months later than the batch record. 15 of these jobs ran on Line 3 nights. 2 ran on Line 1 day shift (21 Oct, 29 Oct; operators D-102 and D-114, permanent staff). Those 2 lots are in the finished-goods warehouse.
28	- All 47 jobs: override = N, printed string identical to payload string, camera result PASS (matched to job data).
29	C2 [stage S1] ERP material-master change history, shelf-life fields, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026 - ERP audit-trail report run by IT, 15 Nov 2026 (system-record): Audit trail for field SHELF_LIFE_M. Each value is stored with a valid-from date.
30	- VT-20-28 and VT-20-56 (Veltranol): new value 36 entered 3 Oct 16:42 by user RA-OKONJO under CC-309, valid-from 01 Mar 2027, with the note 'per approved variation - lots manufactured from 01-03-2027 only'. The existing value of 24 (valid since 2023) was kept and is still the value in effect today.
31	- The other 10 CC-309 edits cover 7 products. Eight of them have a valid-from date equal to the entry date. Two have later dates, both entered 20 Oct with valid-from 01 Jan 2027: HX-15-30 (36 to 24) and MR-05-14 (24 to 30).
32	- No other changes to SHELF_LIFE_M in the period.
33	This report does not include packing history for the products listed.
34	C3 [stage S1] Agency operator induction and competency records, night shift, Sep - Oct 2026 - Training department files (document): Six agency operators (A-201 to A-206) finished induction 26-29 Sep. Four were signed off as competent in labelling setup (SOP PK-044) on 2 Oct and two on 9 Oct. The night supervisor countersigned the two later sign-offs after those operators had already run three jobs each. Assessment notes include 'hesitant at override screen' (A-203) and 'needs reminder to check work-order printout' (A-205). No assessment records an override error.
35	C4 [stage S1] Shift rosters and line assignments, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026 - Workforce management system export (system-record): The rosters list names, shift and line only. Whitcombe was night supervisor throughout. Night-shift overtime rose from 6% of hours in September to 11% in October.

The engineers typed the test inputs by hand. They were not received from PackBridge.
37	C6 [stage S1] Camera reject statistics, Lines 1 and 3, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026 - Camera inspection system reports (telemetry): Line 3 reject rate: 0.31% (Sep), 0.29% (Oct), 0.33% (Nov to date). Last configuration change: 14 Mar 2025 (CC-188, initial go-live). Interface error log: no errors for 1 Sep - 10 Nov.
40	C9 [stage S1] Interview notes, four agency operators, 14 Nov 2026 - HR and QA joint interviews (staff-account): All four say they never overrode an expiry on Veltranol and 'just checked it matched the work order and pressed Confirm'. Under SOP PK-044, work-order printouts are thrown away at the end of each job and are not in the records. QA release reviews on 27 Oct, 30 Oct and 4 Nov say 'record complete'. No carton specimen is kept with the record.
42	C11 [stage S1] CC-309 change-control form and impact assessment - Change-control system (document): Raised by Regulatory Affairs on 22 Sep. Scope: 12 material-master edits across 9 products, arising from the annual product review and approved variations. The edit list is held in the ERP. Impact assessment, section 4, 'Downstream systems': 'Master-data values only. PackBridge applies valid-from dates; no impact on packaging line systems. No line testing required.' Approved by QA and Engineering on 30 Sep. Closed 25 Oct.
43	C12 [stage S1] Line 3 shift handover log, October 2026 - Line 3 handover book (document): October entries mention: printhead cleans (5 Oct, 19 Oct), carton magazine jam (11 Oct), camera re-teach checked OK (2 Oct), agency operator A-205 sent home sick (16 Oct), and 'Veltranol run long, bulk arrived late' (22 Oct). No entry mentions expiry dates, overrides or label queries. Several night entries are initialled but not dated.
44	C13 [stage S1] Line 3 packing-room temperature and humidity records, 1 Sep - 10 Nov 2026 - Building monitoring system (telemetry): Logged every 15 minutes. There were two sensor dropouts (7 Oct 03:10-03:40; 26 Oct 01:00-01:15), and those gaps were filled from the room's second probe. No operator complaints about ink drying were recorded.
45	C14 [stage S1] Brightwell Staffing contract and Q3 2026 supplier review - Procurement file (document): The contract runs Apr 2026 - Mar 2027 for up to ten packaging operators. The agency handles basic GMP induction, and the site handles SOP training and competency. Q3 review: fill rate 94%, two late starts, rated 'meets expectations'. No quality incidents were attributed to agency staff before October. The renewal discussion is set for January 2027.
46	C15 [stage S1] Internal data-integrity audit report, June 2025 - Corporate internal audit (prior-report): Observation 3 (minor): 'Master-data changes are assessed for regulatory impact but not routinely for effect on downstream line systems.' Observation 7: training records were sometimes signed after the activity, rated minor.
47	CANDIDATES
48	H1: Operators entered or overrode the wrong expiry dates during line setup.
49	H2: The printer firmware upgrade changed the expiry dates as they were printed.
50	H3: The wrong expiry dates were already in the data sent to the printers, before any operator action.
51	H4: Wrong expiry dates on Veltranol cartons began before the late-September changes and went undetected.
52	H5: Products other than Veltranol have also been packed with wrong expiry dates.
53	R1: Agency operators joining the night shift (CC-305, 30 Sep) -> Wrong expiry dates printed on Veltranol cartons (causes)
54	R2: Printer firmware upgrade 4.2 to 4.3 (CC-301, 28 Sep) -> Wrong expiry dates printed on Veltranol cartons (causes)
55	R3: Regulatory Affairs' October material-master edits (CC-309) -> Wrong expiry dates printed on Veltranol cartons (causes)
56	A1: Remove the agency operators from labelling duties and issue them formal warnings, as the site director proposes.
57	A2: Reset the Veltranol shelf-life records in the ERP so that only the value approved for current lots can be read. Extend the hold to every Veltranol lot packed since those records last changed. Require a second-person QA check of printed expiry against the approved batch record at each setup until the cause is fully resolved. Inspect retained cartons of any other product whose shelf-life record changed in October.
58	A3: Commission a site-wide reconciliation of printed expiry against batch records for every lot packed in the past 12 months.
59	A4: Begin over-labelling held and warehouse stock of other products with corrected expiry dates, on the assumption that they carry the same fault.
60	A5: Switch off the camera's expiry-field verification on Lines 1 and 3, since it passed every faulty carton and gives false assurance.

answers.justification: C1 shows override = N on all 47 jobs and the printed string identical to the PackBridge payload. Two faulty jobs were set up by permanent day-shift staff on Line 1, and agency-run jobs from 30 Sep to 3 Oct were correct (C1, C9).

C1 shows every printed expiry exactly matched the payload, and 4 jobs after the 28 Sep firmware change printed correctly. The faulty values were already in the payload, with SHELF_LIFE_M = 36 (C1, C5).

From 4 Oct the payload carried SHELF_LIFE_M = 36 and a 12-month-late expiry before any operator action (C1). This followed the ERP entry of 36 on 3 Oct with valid-from 01 Mar 2027, which PackBridge evidently read despite USE_VALID_FROM = Y (C2, C8).
All 30 Veltranol jobs from 2 Jun to 3 Oct had SHELF_LIFE_M = 24 and expiries that matched the batch record (C1). That counters the QA manager's suspicion in E6.

C2 shows two other products (HX-15-30, MR-05-14) were given future-dated shelf-life values on 20 Oct, so they are exposed to the same mechanism. C2 explicitly excludes packing history and no printer data for those products is in evidence, so this is live but unestablished.

Agency operators set up 3 correct Line 3 night jobs from 30 Sep to 3 Oct, faulty jobs also occurred on Line 1 day shift with permanent staff, and no overrides occurred (C1, C4, C9). The Line 3 nights clustering is coincidental with the product schedule.
Correct expiries were printed after the firmware change, and every printed string matched its payload (C1). The fault onset tracks the ERP edit rather than the 28 Sep upgrade (C2).

The ERP value of 36 was entered 3 Oct 16:42 under CC-309 and the first wrong job ran 4 Oct 22:10 (C2, C1). Payloads then carried 36 on every line and shift, operator and firmware rivals are excluded (C1), and CC-309 skipped downstream testing (C11, C15).
The evidence clears the agency operators (C1, C9). Disciplining them punishes the wrong party and leaves the master-data/PackBridge cause active, so further mislabelled lots would follow (C2, C8).

A2 removes the active data cause (C2), contains all affected lots (C1 Line 1 warehouse lots and C7 hand-booked lots), adds an independent check that the camera cannot give (E4, C10), and targets the other future-dated records (C2).

Reconciling 12 months of lots site-wide is a reasonable scope check because PackBridge has run since Mar 2025 (C8) and earlier future-dated edits are not covered by C2. However, C1 shows the fault starting in October, so this is broader and slower than the targeted containment in A2.

Other products are not confirmed affected (C2 has no packing history), and HX-15-30's change would shorten rather than extend expiry. Blanket over-labelling on assumption is not justified until printer records are checked.

The camera correctly checks that the print matches the job data and catches truncated or smudged codes, rejecting 412 truncated cartons (C6, E4). Switching it off disables a working protective control and would not fix the data fault.
C1, C2 and C8 together establish the data-path cause and rule out operator and firmware causes, which is enough to commit to A2's correction and containment.

ambiguousItems: I-A3: acceptable vs premature. C1 bounds the Veltranol fault to October, but PackBridge's apparent disregard of valid-from dates may predate the C2 window (live since Mar 2025), so a broader look is partly justified.
I-H5: unknown vs supported. The same mechanism plausibly hit MR-05-14 and HX-15-30, but no packing evidence is given.
I-R1: contradicted vs association-only. Faulty jobs cluster on Line 3 nights, but C1 directly counters a causal link.
caseProblems: C1 and C2 together leave no uncertainty, so the case is close to deterministic. Only the hidden PackBridge defect (USE_VALID_FROM = Y yet the future value was read) is left unexplained, and it contradicts the vendor statement in E5 without any explanation being offered.
C2's line 'the existing value of 24 ... is still the value in effect today' practically gives away H3/R3.

A2 says 'reset records so only the current value can be read', which presumes the mechanism. That is fine, but it is the only action written in detailed, well-scoped terms, which cues it as the correct answer.
